concepts.name: DNA copying and variation
concepts.description: Reproduction copies the DNA blueprint along with extra cell apparatus; copying is never perfectly accurate, so offspring vary slightly, and variation helps a species survive when its niche changes.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §7.1-7.1.1, p.113-114 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Fission
concepts.description: Unicellular organisms reproduce by cell division: binary fission into two (bacteria, Amoeba in any plane, Leishmania in a set orientation) or multiple fission into many cells at once (Plasmodium).
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §7.2.1, p.115-116 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Fragmentation, regeneration and budding
concepts.description: Spirogyra breaks into fragments that each grow; Hydra and Planaria regenerate whole organisms from pieces using specialised cells; Hydra and yeast also reproduce by buds that detach.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §7.2.2-7.2.4, p.116-117 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Vegetative propagation
concepts.description: Roots, stems or leaves grow into new plants (layering, grafting, Bryophyllum leaf buds); such plants flower earlier, keep the parent's characteristics and include seedless kinds; tissue culture grows many from one.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §7.2.5, p.117-118 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Spore formation
concepts.description: In bread mould (Rhizopus) the sporangia hold spores with thick protective walls that grow into new individuals on a moist surface; the threads are hyphae.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §7.2.6, p.118 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Why sexual reproduction
concepts.description: Combining DNA from two individuals creates new combinations of variants faster; meiosis halves the chromosome number in germ-cells so fertilisation restores it; gametes specialise into a motile male and a food-storing female gamete.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §7.3-7.3.1, p.119-120 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Sexual reproduction in flowering plants
concepts.description: Stamens (pollen) and pistil (ovary, style, stigma) are the reproductive parts; self- and cross-pollination; a pollen tube reaches the ovule for fertilisation; the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary a fruit; germination.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §7.3.2, p.120-121 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Puberty and human reproductive systems
concepts.description: Changes at puberty signal sexual maturation; the male system (testes, vas deferens, prostate, seminal vesicles, urethra) and female system (ovaries, oviducts, uterus, vagina); fertilisation in the oviduct; the placenta nourishes the embryo.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §7.3.3, p.121-124 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Menstruation
concepts.description: One egg is released each month and the uterus lining thickens to receive it; if the egg is not fertilised, the lining breaks down and leaves as blood and mucus, roughly monthly, for two to eight days.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §7.3.3(c), p.124 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Reproductive health and contraception
concepts.description: Readiness for sex and parenthood, sexually transmitted infections (gonorrhoea, syphilis, warts, HIV-AIDS), contraception (condoms, pills, copper-T, surgery), and protecting the sex ratio against female foeticide.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §7.3.3(d), p.124-125 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)
